items.summary: 16.01.01:220 invented a suppression trigger — 'suppressed from search at the floor (16.01.05 D-03)' — that its cited decision does not contain and that 16.05.05 D-02/D-08 flatly contradict ('presentation, not suppression'). Applied literally it would delist the cold-start majority (16.01.01:215) and every trades record, which live at the floor permanently (16.05.05:81, 16.01.07 DT-02). Rewrote the row to state the canonical rule: the floor labels and does not suppress; suppression is reserved for `possibly closed`, which requires 2 distinct-account corroborations + 21-day silence (16.01.05 D-06). No new value invented — the threshold is quoted from the owning file.

items.summary: 16.06.03 owns the reservation lifecycle and ratified D-12, explicitly superseding the block model and recording the supersession in D-13. 16.01.02:181 and its cross-cut note at :239 still carried the pre-D-12 text ('It is a block, not a booking ... no harvest trigger'), and the same stale statement had been copied into 16.03.01:202 and :288 citing 16.01.02 as precedent. Swept all four to the canonical model: zero-value reservation, no deposit/ladder/payment, consumes inventory, completes, fires the harvest at `owner` class per 16.05.06 D-11 — with 16.06.03 DT-12's carve-out preserved verbatim (a block is still right for a private event, which is not a session). The 'second instance of domain Q-10' framing in both files is now marked closed by 16.06.03 D-13, leaving lockout as the open instance, which matches domain index Q-10.
